name: Pull-Up
grip: Overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width, palms facing away from the athlete.
description: Pull bodyweight vertically to an overhead bar using a wide overhand pronated grip until the chin clears the bar, building classic V-taper latissimus width and upper body pulling strength.
setup: Grasp an overhead pull-up bar with a pronated overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Hang freely in a full dead hang with arms completely extended and shoulders actively engaged.
Brace your core, cross your ankles slightly behind you or keep legs straight with toes pointed.
instructions: Initiate the movement by depressing your scapulae, then pull your body upward by driving your elbows down and out toward your ribs.
Keep your chest lifted and pull until your chin comfortably clears the top of the bar.
Pause for a brief count at the top peak contraction, squeezing your lats.
Lower your body smoothly under complete control back to a full dead hang with arms fully extended before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Drive elbows down to your ribs.
Chest to the bar, chin over.
Full dead hang at the bottom on every rep.
commonMistakes: Kipping, swinging, or bicycling the legs to generate momentum.
Cutting the bottom range of motion short without full elbow extension.
Reaching the chin up with cervical hyperextension rather than pulling the chest to the bar.

logging.example: Bodyweight: record repetitions performed (or note added external weight if dipping belt is used).
logging.note: Strict bodyweight pull-up; count clean repetitions from dead hang to chin-over-bar.

variantNote: Canonical pronated vertical pull-up. The overhand grip emphasizes frontal plane shoulder adduction, placing primary emphasis on the latissimus dorsi and teres major.
